The cluster_density feature measures: fraction of other unvisited cities within mean distance of the candidate.

- High cluster_density (close to 1): most unvisited cities are close to this candidate
- Low cluster_density (close to 0): few unvisited cities are close to this candidate

When we visit a candidate with high cluster_density:
- We've "used up" a position that has many good next-step options
- Future moves from this position can be short

When we visit a candidate with low cluster_density:
- We've moved to an isolated location
- Future moves will likely be longer

So visiting high-density candidates first is generally good. This is a valid local-distance refinement.

For nearest-neighbor-style selection, regret tells us: if I don't pick this candidate now, will I have good chances to pick it later? High regret means it's hard to come back to this candidate later (because its nearest unvisited neighbor is much closer than its second nearest).
